title.narrative: Umut Women´s Community Assistance and Solidarity Association

description.narrative: The project is implemented in Turkey and Syria. The main outcome areas it contributes to are countering the threats to democracy and human rights, promoting peace and dialogue to mitigate armed conflict and social tensions and opposing the backlash to increase gender equality. The main rights holders are members of the Syrian Women's Network which consist of individuals and civil society organisations, and women affected by war in various forms. Through support to awareness raising campaigns, capacity building activities, network meetings, gender mainstreamaning of the peace processes, policies and legislation and monitoring of violations of women's rights the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsCentral project: - The project is a cooperation between Syrian Women's Network and the Palme Center. Syrian Women's Network Syrian Women's Network has a general assembly composed of approximately 21 member organisations, all Syrian civil society organisations, and 170 individual members. The network was formed as a result of two conferences that the Olof Palme International Center hosted during the period 2011-2013, and was established in May 2013. Its target group is the Syrian civil and political actors who work for gender equality, social change, democracy and human rights. Its office is located in Gaziantep in Turkey, but implements activities in Lebanon, Syria and Turkey.Other Donors to the OrganisationN/AProject ObjectiveProject objective: - Contribute to setting policies and legal frameworks that support the role of women in the local, national and international political scene. - Introducing an initial draft of legal amendments to the Constitution, preventive mechanisms, monitoring and accountability procedures to ensure women's rights. - Granting justice, equality, and compensation to women affected by the war and reintegrate them into society.Actor groupsDecision-makers: The Syrian government, the juridical system and decision makers on a local level. Actor working in cooperation: International and local civil society and peace building committees. Right holders: Members of the network and CSOs, and women in the communities that are targeted by the project.
